contexts.text: He has seen that brutes have a life almost like that of men...
Make themselves out to be like brutes...
The love of the young exists also with all brutes, even the worst...

He confirms himself by the fact that brute animals also live, but still do not live after death... This is because he lives in corporeal and sensuous things, which life regarded in itself is scarcely different from the life of brute animals; the sole difference being that the man can think and reason about the things which come in his way, and he does not then reflect upon this faculty which he enjoys above brute animals.
Moreover love to God and the neighbour ought to be the life of a man, by which he should be distinguished from brute animals.
If he did not learn these things, man would be much worse than a brute animal.
Under Man, see these references. AC 5160:end. AC 7604:end. AC 8604. TCR 380:3. TCR 417. SE 2209. SE 2854.
That which is called a brute and a stock.
On the life of brutes. General article.
(The sense by which brutes find their way home.)
Brute animals live according to the order of their nature, and therefore have no need for Spirits to be with them.
Evil spirits are just like brutes which have a faculty of reasoning, thus like rational brutes. General article... Of themselves they are much lower than brutes.

If the brutes had needed shoes and garments, they would have made them much better than men, as is evident from their nests... But as they have no need of them they have no skill in them, wherefore the life of the brutes is such as it is because they are corporeal... Thus we may conclude that such things as appertain to the body are the things which we have in common with beasts.
